message.content:
The plasma membrane is a protein‑rich “gatekeeper” that controls what enters and leaves the cell. It contains a wide variety of proteins that can be broadly grouped into a few functional classes: | Functional class | Typical roles | Representative proteins (examples) | |------------------|---------------|------------------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often form channels, carriers, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Voltage‑gated Na⁺ channel (Nav1.5)**
• **Voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv1.3)**
• **Aquaporin‑1** (water channel)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)**
• **Glucose transporter 4 (GLUT4)**
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin, chemokine receptors (CCR5, CXCR4)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** – e.g., EGFR, HER2 | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via lipid anchors or protein‑protein interactions. | • **Src family kinases** (e.g., Src, Lyn)
• **Phospholipase C‑γ**
• **Caveolin‑1** (caveolae scaffold)
• **Annexins** (Ca²⁺‑dependent phospholipid binding) | | **Adhesion molecules** | Mediate cell–cell or cell–matrix contacts. | • **Integrins** (α5β1, αvβ3)
• **Cadherins** (E‑cadherin, N‑cadherin)
• **Selectins** (L‑selectin, E‑selectin) | | **Immune‑system markers** | Serve as surface antigens for immune recognition. | • **CD45** (protein tyrosine phosphatase)
• **CD3** (T‑cell receptor complex)
• **CD4** (helper T‑cell coreceptor)
• **CD8** (cytotoxic T‑cell coreceptor)
• **MHC class I & II molecules** | | **Enzymes** | Catalyze reactions at the membrane surface. | • **Alkaline phosphatase**
• **Phosphatidylinositol‑3‑kinase (PI3K)** (membrane‑associated) | | **Transporters & exchangers** | Move solutes across the membrane. | • **Sodium‑glucose cotransporter 1 (SGLT1)**
• **Calcium‑ATPase (SERCA)** (though mainly ER, some isoforms are on the plasma membrane)
• **Monocarboxylate transporters (MCT1, MCT4)** | ### How many proteins are there? The human plasma membrane contains **thousands** of distinct proteins. The exact number depends on cell type, developmental stage, and physiological conditions. For a more exhaustive, cell‑type‑specific list you can query a proteomics database or use a tool such as the `cellbio_get_proteins` function (e.g., `cellbio_get_proteins({"cell_compartment":"plasma membrane"})`). --- #### Quick Take‑away - **Integral proteins**: channels, pumps, transporters, receptors. - **Peripheral proteins**: signaling adaptors, enzymes, structural scaffolds. - **Adhesion molecules**: integrins, cadherins, selectins. - **Immune markers**: CD proteins, MHC molecules. These proteins together give the plasma membrane its dynamic, multifunctional character.
